claims.text: Firefly Wedding premieres October 9, 2026. The Japanese broadcast begins at 11:30 p.m. JST on Fuji TV’s Noitamina block, while Crunchyroll has confirmed worldwide streaming as the anime airs.
Firefly Wedding premieres October 9, 2026 as part of Crunchyroll's Fall 2026 lineup. The anime is produced by david production.

The story follows Satoko, a noblewoman in poor health who becomes the target of an assassin. Trying to survive, she makes an extraordinary marriage proposal to Shinpei, turning a kidnapping into a dangerous relationship built around a false wedding and increasingly complicated feelings.
david production is producing the anime. Takahiro Kamei directs, Yuko Kakihara handles series composition and scripts, Yukiko Aikei is credited for character designs, and NOGRID composes the music.
Episode 1 premieres October 9. AniNextUp will track subsequent episode dates and add exact simulcast times only when they are officially confirmed.

Crunchyroll has announced worldwide streaming as the series airs. Catalog availability can still differ by territory, so viewers should check the local Crunchyroll listing near premiere time. You can also browse the AniNextUp streaming hub for other Fall 2026 releases.
Three new My Happy Marriage special episodes premiere October 25, 2026, with Netflix among the announced streaming services.
All three special episodes premiere October 25, 2026. TOKYO MX begins the earliest Japanese television broadcast at 7:00 p.m. JST, running the three episodes together through 8:30 p.m.

The official Japanese schedule says streaming begins progressively from 8:30 p.m. JST on October 25. Netflix is among the listed services, alongside d Anime Store, ABEMA, U-NEXT, Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu and others in Japan.
Netflix Anime has announced the three specials for October 25. Regional catalog timing can vary, but Netflix is the principal confirmed international destination promoted for the release.

Miyo and Kiyoka's relationship continues as their wedding draws closer. The official teaser shows Miyo attending a cooking class with Hazuki, where she encounters an old classmate, while the couple also faces new family and personal challenges.
The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 premiered October 2, 2026. Here is the confirmed split-cour release schedule, where to watch it, the official trailer and when the second cour returns.

The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 premiered in Japan on October 2, 2026. The official anime portal lists the main broadcast every Friday at 11:00 p.m. JST on Nippon TV's nationwide Friday Anime Night block.
The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 release date was October 2, 2026 for its first cour. The second cour is officially scheduled for April 2027.

The third season is a split-cour release. Its first cour begins in October 2026, while the official schedule places the second cour in April 2027. That means the story continues after a seasonal break rather than running straight through without interruption.

Episode 2 of Season 3 (episode 50 overall) is scheduled for Friday, October 9, 2026, at 11:00 p.m. JST on Nippon TV in Japan, according to the official anime broadcast calendar. Crunchyroll lists its subtitled Season 3 episodes on Fridays at 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time in supported territories; check the local service listing for regional availability and schedule changes.

For the upcoming Japanese broadcast, the official calendar also lists episode 51 on October 16, episode 52 on October 23 and episode 53 on October 30 at 11:40 p.m. JST. See the official broadcast and streaming schedule and Crunchyroll Fall 2026 lineup for updates.

The official Japanese portal says streaming platforms begin carrying episodes progressively after the television broadcast. Crunchyroll carries Season 3 in supported international territories; availability and episode timing can differ by region.

The new story moves Maomao and Jinshi beyond the familiar confines of the rear palace. Official material teases signs of a disaster threatening the country, a mysterious shrine maiden and new responsibilities for Jinshi. Those developments push the mystery into a broader setting while keeping Maomao's investigative perspective at the center.

Season 3 is not the franchise's only major 2026 release. The first theatrical film is scheduled for December 11 in Japan with a new story concept by original author Natsu Hyuuga. See our Apothecary Diaries movie guide and December 2026 anime calendar for the confirmed movie details.
Yes. The first cour begins in October 2026 and the second cour is scheduled for April 2027.
Yes. Season 3 continues Maomao and Jinshi's existing story and builds on mysteries and relationships established in the earlier seasons.
Black Clover Season 2 arrives as one of October’s major anime releases. Streaming availability may vary by region.
Black Clover Season 2 premiered on October 3, 2026. The official Japanese site lists the new television season for Saturdays at 11:00 p.m. JST on the TV Tokyo network and other stations.

The new season began Saturday, October 3 at 23:00 JST in Japan. This return brings the television anime back with a new run following the earlier Black Clover series and the franchise's subsequent movie.

Crunchyroll is carrying the season in supported international regions. Streaming availability, subtitles, dubs and episode-release times can vary by country, so the exact listing should be checked in the viewer's regional catalog.

Asta and the Magic Knights return as the story moves deeper into the conflicts surrounding the Clover and Spade kingdoms. The official Season 2 campaign includes a new promotional video and updated character material, positioning the return as a major continuation rather than a recap project.
The Japanese television slot is scheduled weekly on Saturdays. AniNextUp will continue tracking the international streaming schedule and any official changes to broadcast timing.
No. The new season continues the existing Black Clover anime story rather than starting over.
Crunchyroll carries the season in supported international territories. Availability, subtitles, dubs and release times can vary by country.
Suikoden: The Anime is tracked in AniNextUp’s October release coverage. Platform availability may differ by territory.
Suikoden: The Anime premiered in Japan on October 3, 2026. The official anime site confirms a nationwide rollout across 32 Japanese stations, including TOKYO MX, Kansai TV and BS Asahi.

The television broadcast begins October 3, with stations joining the schedule progressively. The premiere is an expanded 60-minute first episode, giving the adaptation extra room to establish its characters, political conflict and world.

The official production has announced distribution across 24 streaming platforms in Japan. International availability can differ by territory, so AniNextUp will distinguish confirmed regional services rather than assuming that every platform carries the series worldwide.

The adaptation draws from the world and central conflict of Konami's classic Suikoden II. The story follows young characters caught in a war that tests old friendships and loyalties, bringing the RPG's large-scale political drama to television.

The production released multiple promotional videos ahead of broadcast, including a third PV in September. The official campaign also confirmed the ending theme, “closed eye sun (feat. Honoka Takahashi)” by Koji Nakamura.

Suikoden has a long-running game legacy, so this anime is both an entry point for newcomers and a new adaptation for existing fans. We will keep this guide focused on confirmed broadcast and streaming information as additional international distribution details are announced.
Blue Box returns with Season 2 on October 4, 2026. AniNextUp tracks the release and regional streaming availability.
Blue Box Season 2 premieres October 4, 2026 on Netflix, with new episodes scheduled weekly.

Season 2 starts October 4, 2026 on Netflix, with new episodes weekly. The exact local release time can vary by region, so viewers should check their Netflix listing for the episode time in their territory.
Taiki Inomata and Chinatsu Kano return as their sports ambitions and slowly developing relationship face a new complication: Yumeka, a former basketball teammate whose arrival shakes up the story.
Netflix is the streaming home for the new season. Netflix's official September 15 announcement confirms an October 4 premiere and weekly episodes.
Taiki and Chinatsu return as they continue balancing competition and their growing relationship. Season 2 also introduces Yumeka, whose connection to Chinatsu adds a new complication to the story.
Yes. Season 2 continues Taiki and Chinatsu's relationship and sports story directly, so newcomers should start with Season 1.
Yes. Netflix confirms new episodes weekly starting October 4, 2026.

Reborn as a Space Mercenary is scheduled in AniNextUp’s Fall 2026 calendar for October 4.

Reborn as a Space Mercenary: I Woke Up Piloting the Strongest Starship! premieres October 4, 2026. Crunchyroll begins streaming the first episode on Sunday alongside the Japanese release, and an English dub launches the same day.

Crunchyroll carries the series in supported international territories. The announced distribution covers most of the world outside Japan, China, Korea and Mongolia, although catalog availability can still vary by location.

After waking in the universe of his favorite science-fiction game, Satou Takahiro takes on the identity of mercenary Hiro. Instead of a conventional fantasy isekai adventure, his new life revolves around starships, space battles, colonies and dangerous jobs across an interstellar setting.
Yes. Crunchyroll confirmed a same-day English dub beginning October 4. Kyle Phillips voices Hiro, with Kelsey Cruz as Elma, Emily Neves as Mimi and Jaclyn Thomas as Serena.

The series mixes the reincarnation framework common to isekai with space-opera and game mechanics. That makes it one of the season's more unusual genre combinations for viewers looking beyond fantasy-world settings.
PSYREN joins the Fall 2026 anime schedule on October 5. Check local availability as release timing can differ by territory.
The long-awaited anime adaptation of PSYREN premieres October 5, 2026. Crunchyroll lists the international simulcast for 7:30 a.m. PT, outside Japan and China.

Crunchyroll has confirmed the international simulcast for October 5 at 7:30 a.m. PT, available worldwide outside Japan and China. In Japan, the TV broadcast starts at 11:00 p.m. JST and participating Japanese streaming services begin from 11:30 p.m. JST.
Episode 1 begins the anime on October 5. Crunchyroll has confirmed the premiere time, while AniNextUp will add later episode dates only as official scheduling information becomes available.

Ageha Yoshina’s life changes after he finds a mysterious red phone card and his childhood friend Sakurako Amamiya disappears. His search pulls him into a deadly mystery connected to the secret organization known as Psyren.

The series will stream internationally on Crunchyroll in supported regions, worldwide outside Japan and China. In Japan, the official site lists services including Prime Video, Hulu, U-NEXT, ABEMA and others from October 5 at 11:30 p.m. JST, with some services potentially using different start times.

PSYREN is a new adaptation, so you do not need to watch an earlier anime first. It adapts Toshiaki Iwashiro's completed Weekly Shonen Jump manga, which ran for 16 collected volumes. The production has also announced that the anime is intended to adapt the original manga through its ending.

Satelight produces the animation. Katsumi Ono directs, Shin Yoshida handles series composition, Akira Okuma is responsible for character designs, and the music team includes Takashi Ohmama, Tatsuhiko Saiki and Shu Kanematsu.
No. This is the first TV anime adaptation of Toshiaki Iwashiro's manga.
No. The anime begins Ageha Yoshina's story from the start, so newcomers can begin with Episode 1.
Yes. The production has announced plans to adapt the original manga through its conclusion.
Crunchyroll lists the dub airtime as TBA. AniNextUp will update this guide when a release date is announced.

Ranma 1/2 Season 3 is part of AniNextUp’s October 2026 coverage. Streaming availability and exact release timing can vary by region.

Ranma 1/2 Season 3 premiered in Japan on October 3, 2026. The official anime site lists the Nippon TV broadcast for Saturdays at 24:55 JST, with nationwide broadcasts following across the Nippon TV network.

The third season began on October 3 in Japan. Because Japanese late-night schedules sometimes write times after midnight using an extended clock, the listed 24:55 slot corresponds to 12:55 a.m. on the following calendar day in standard notation.

Netflix is the key streaming destination for the new season. The official production announcement says episodes stream exclusively on Netflix immediately after the Japanese television broadcast. Exact availability and release timing can still differ by country, so viewers should check their regional Netflix catalog.

The official Season 3 key visual brings Ranma, Akane and Ryoga together with characters appearing in the new run. The remake continues the martial-arts romantic comedy built around Ranma and Akane, with new rivals and complications expanding the ensemble around them.

Yes. The Japanese broadcast is scheduled weekly on Saturdays, and the official announcement places Netflix streaming immediately after broadcast. AniNextUp will keep tracking schedule changes and regional availability as the season progresses.
Yes. Season 3 continues the current Ranma 1/2 remake rather than restarting the story, so watching Seasons 1 and 2 first provides the character relationships and ongoing story context.
Netflix is the confirmed streaming destination, with availability and episode timing depending on the viewer's regional catalog.
